intro_1: Bellwether, 1988. The 6:15 bus drops Nico Vale at the end of Kettle Street. His first time home in two years.
Protection fee, grandma. Same as last week.
So I pay you to protect me from you. And if I don't pay, you protect me from you by... not protecting me from you?
Delivery! For whoever's about to get punched.
intro_hint_1: Move with {move}. {punch} Punch, {kick} Kick, {jump} Jump. Chain Punches into a combo!
intro_2: Nico Vale. Look at you. Still punching above your weight class.
Hi, Dot. Still sassing guys twice your size?
Somebody has to. Those Chain Dogs have been leaning on every shop on the street for a month.
I'm looking for Eli. He sent me a postcard. 'Come home. Need someone I trust.'
Hon... Eli's been gone four days. He came in Thursday white as a sheet, hugging some notebook. Ordered coffee and didn't touch it.
Mara's been tearing the town apart looking for him. She's at her garage on Brickrow Lane, just east of here.
Go. And come back for pie. The diner's always open to you, hon.
mara_meet: If that's another Chain Dog, I've got a wrench with your name on it.
Nico?! Two years, and you just walk in like you went out for milk?
Two years of no calls. No letters. And you show up NOW?
...He wrote you. Figures. He's been weird for weeks. Late nights, new shoes, wouldn't say where the money came from.
Thursday he slid a note under my door. 'If I don't come back, the Chain Dogs know where the book went. Don't go after it. Luv you, M.'
He spelled 'love' wrong. He only does that when he's scared.
Obviously. The Chain Dogs hang out in the Chain Lot at the end of Brickrow. Their boss is Duke Brannigan. Big mohawk, bigger mouth.
Here. Twenty bucks for food. Dot will fix you up, and Coach Benny still sells fighting manuals at the rec center down the lane.
When have I ever been stupid?
You want that list alphabetical or chronological?
duke_intro: Well, well. The delivery boy. You know how many of my pups you put in the gutter today?
Mercer? Skinny, glasses, cries a lot? We jumped him Thursday. Guy in a gray coat paid us to grab his bag.
Bag was full of nothing. Kid ripped the pages out. So now I'm out a payday AND I'm in a bad mood.
Chain Dogs don't lose on our own turf!
duke_defeat: Okay! OKAY! Uncle! You hit like a garbage truck.
Sold it to the Pike sisters at the Canal Market. They fence anything. Gray-coat guy wanted it bad, so they figured they'd jack the price.
Look... that gray coat. He paid us to scare Kettle Street. Break windows. Make folks want to move. I didn't ask why.
You never ask why, Duke. That's your whole problem.
Here. Key to the underpass. And tell Dot... tell her the windows are on me.
bus_unlocked: With the Chain Dogs off the streets, the River Line buses are running again. Bus stops let you travel between districts you've visited.
jett_intro: Hold up, hero. Word on the Mile is somebody's paying top dollar for a certain courier bag.
Word on the street is you're in my way.
Ooh, he's got lines. Name's Jett Vance. Fastest feet on the Neon Mile.
Let's see what the Old Quarter's got.
jett_retreat: Okay, okay, you're decent! I've got a date with some rooftops.
Catch you on the Mile, Delivery Boy!
Jett vaults the railing, lands on a passing barge, and is gone.
pikes_intro: Customers pay, Rhea. This one's got that 'I'm about to make a scene' face.
Eli Mercer's satchel. Duke says you bought it.
Bought it, cleaned it, priced it. Two hundred dollars.
How about a discount on getting beaten up?
Funny doesn't pay rent. Get him!
pikes_defeat: Fine! FINE! Take the stupid bag! It smells like fish anyway. Everything smells like fish.
There wasn't any ledger in it, if that's what you're after. Just route sheets and a photo.
Inside the satchel: Eli's delivery manifests. Envelopes to Switch House 4 at the Ironworks, every one signed 'V.R.' And a polaroid of Eli with an older rail worker.
That's Gus Pereira. Switchman. Nice guy. Haven't seen him at the market in a week.
We'll lower the drawbridge. Just... go away. And buy a fish sometime.
act2_card: ACT II: THE IRONWORKS. Heavy Yard Boys shrug off light hits while they wind up. Hit them with finishers, kicks and throws, or get out of the way.
switch_hint: Otto's Yard Boys are guarding someone in the back. Clear them out!
gus_rescue: You're not one of Otto's boys. Who are you?
Eli... that kid. He delivered envelopes here every Friday. Cash. Payroll for Otto's crew, straight from Greyline Development.
The company buying up every block from here to the river. Folks who won't sell get visits. Fires. Broken windows. Rail-side houses 'condemned.'
Eli figured it out. He asked me to testify. Next thing I know, Otto's boys lock me in here so I won't talk.
Otto keeps the payroll book in the foundry office. That's your proof. The foundry's at the east end of the Rail Spur. I'll unbolt the door for you.
My brother runs a bait shop out on Floodgate Road. I'll lie low there. Thank you, son.
otto_intro: Pereira's out. Mercer's buddy is in my foundry. Somebody's getting docked a week's pay.
Greyline's paying you to burn people out of their homes, Otto.
I'm paid to keep the line moving. What happens down the line ain't my business.
It's my neighborhood. That makes it my business.
otto_defeat: Hrrgh... okay. You win. Rook's gonna... ugh.
Victor Rook. Greyline's fixer. Gray coat, nice gloves, scary calm. He signs the checks, and the Starlight Arcade on the Neon Mile counts the cash. Back room.
Victor Rook. Everybody on Kettle Street knows that name. The best fighter the Old Quarter ever had. The man who taught Nico and Eli to throw a punch.
Take the payroll. And the tunnel key. The rail tunnel runs straight back to Brickrow Lane. I'm done.
neon_hint: The Neon Saints leap in with jump kicks. Guard them, or meet them in the air.
arcade_jett: Delivery Boy?! Didn't think you'd make it this far east.
The back room, Jett. The count book. Hand it over.
How do you even... ugh. Okay. You want it?
Come get it! Rooftops! If you can keep up!
Jett bolts out the door with a ledger under his arm. The fire escape is at the east end of Arcade Alley.
jett_intro2: Welcome to my office. Best view in Bellwether.
Why are you working for Rook, Jett?
Working FOR? I don't work for anybody. Rook pays me to keep the Mile quiet. Easy money.
Quiet. Like the families getting burned out of the rail houses? Like Eli?
jett_defeat: Man... nobody's ever kept up with me before.
Rook's paying you to scare your own people.
I know. I KNOW, okay? I found out last week. My grandma's building on Velvet Street got a Greyline notice.
I was going to bail. I just didn't know how. Here. The count book. Every payment to every gang, in Rook's handwriting.
And take this. My lucky bandana. Never been beaten till today, so... maybe it's your luck now.
Get the proof somewhere safe, Delivery Boy. When you're ready to hit Rook, the whole Mile will be there.
Mister Nico! MISTER NICO! Mara called the newsstand! She said get back to the garage, fast! Something's wrong!
setback_arrive: Smoke curls out of Quinn Garage. Men in gray jackets are hauling boxes out the roll-up door.
Well, look who came home. Mr. Rook says hello.
Inside. Mostly fine. Get him, boys.
setback_garage: They took everything, Nico. The manifests. The payroll. The count book. They knew exactly what to look for.
My ARM is fine! My GARAGE is not fine! I told you not to drag...
...No. That's not fair. Eli dragged us. You came because he asked. Like you always do.
Don't be sorry. Be smart. You think I'd leave evidence lying around? I photocopied every page. They're in the spare tire.
rook_garage: I taught you that stance. Chin's still too high.
This neighborhood is dying, Nico. The mill closed. The rail's half dead. Greyline is going to build something new here, and I'm making sure it happens in an orderly way.
Orderly? You're burning people out of their homes.
I'm moving them along before the people who don't care do it worse. You left. I stayed. Somebody has to manage the ending.
Eli is safe. For now. He made a choice, Nico. Ask him about it, if you ever see him again.
Rook buttons his coat and walks out into the rain.
...What did he mean, Eli made a choice?
There's something else. This was taped inside the tire with the copies. Eli's handwriting on the label.
A cassette. Eli's voice crackles from Mara's shop radio: 'If they take me, it's the Floodgate warehouse. Rook's place by the river.'
Go get Jett and his crew. Floodgate Road is past the Neon Mile rooftops. I'll fix the tow truck and meet you at the warehouse. Don't argue.
act3_card: ACT III: THE UNDERLINE. Coach Benny has a new manual for you, and Mara's workbench can go all the way now.
alliance: Delivery Boy! Told you the whole Mile would show up.
Plus us. Rook's people stiffed us on the satchel money. Then they kicked over our fish.
And the Chain Dogs! Well. Me. The pups are grounded.
Is that... the Backstreet Oath? Man, I haven't heard that since Benny's junior league.
Rook taught it to us. Time somebody reminded him. Here they come!
alliance_done: Bridge is ours. We'll hold it. Go on.
I'm sticking with you, Delivery Boy. Somebody's gotta make you look good.
price_meet: Hold it. Officer Dana Price, Bellwether PD. You're the kid tearing up half the city.
Relax. I've been trying to build a case against Greyline for a year. Every witness gets scared off. Every file goes missing.
We've got copies of the payroll and the count book.
Copies won't stick. Rook's lawyers will call them forgeries. I need his original ledger. Get me that, and I can make arrests.
I'll be outside the warehouse with backup. Officially, I never met you.
sabine_intro: Captain Holt, Greyline Security. This is private property. Turn around.
Mr. Rook has a lot of things inside. My job is the fence. Not the why.
Everybody keeps saying that. 'Not my business.' 'Not the why.'
sabine_defeat: He told us we were keeping order. Clearing squatters. Then I saw the files. Families. Kids.
Here's the gate key. Mercer is in the holding office past the storage floor.
And Vale... Rook keeps the ledger on him. Always.
I'll keep the Gray Jackets busy out here. Go get your friend.
mara_arrives: Headlights. An engine roar. Mara's patched-up tow truck smashes straight through the loading dock gate.
Is attached to the steering wheel. I'm fine. Price is outside with half the police force pretending they're not here.
eli_found: N-Nico? Is that actually you, or did they finally hit me hard enough?
Mara hugs him hard enough to make him wheeze.
I deserve that. Nico... there's something I have to tell you.
Mom's hospital bills. Forty thousand dollars. The bank was going to take the house. Then Rook offered me a delivery job. Envelopes. Good money. No questions.
So I didn't ask any. For three months. Then the Hendersons' house on Rail Street burned, the same week I dropped an envelope at Otto's.
I copied his ledger. Every page I could. I tried to get it to the paper, and they grabbed me on the way.
Because you left, Nico. And I was ashamed. I wrote you anyway.
Group hug later. Ledger now. Price needs the original.
Rook keeps it on him. And there's a safe in his office full of deeds Greyline forged. Mara, help me crack it. Nico...
He's on the main floor, through that door. He'll be waiting. He always waits.
rook_intro: You came alone. Good. I hate crowds.
I'm not alone. Nobody fights alone. You taught us that.
I taught a lot of kids a lot of things. Most of them grew up and left. The ones who stayed got eaten.
I didn't burn this neighborhood, Nico. Time did. I'm just the man holding the match.
Chin down. Hands up. Let's see what you remember.
rook_phase2: Rook peels off his coat and pulls a steel pipe from a rack. Overhead, the warehouse crane groans to life.
Watch for red shadows: falling crates! The crates they leave behind can be picked up and thrown.
rook_defeat: Take it. It was always going to end with somebody taking it. I'm glad it was you.
Eli, Mara and Officer Price burst through the door.
Victor Rook, you're under arrest for arson, extortion and conspiracy. You have the right to remain silent.
The safe was full of forged deeds. Every 'sale' on Kettle Street. Price has all of it.
Somebody had to make the delivery.
ending_diner: Well, look at this. A full house. First time in a year.
Dot, can I get a coffee? I promise I'll drink this one.
On the house. Everything's on the house tonight.
Everything? Then I'll have one of everything.
So, Nico. You staying this time?
Somebody's got to keep an eye on you two.
Nico pulls a battered clipboard out of his jacket.
Oh, Dot. Delivery. One neighborhood. Slightly dented. Sign here.
postgame_welcome: THE END... of the story. Bellwether is yours to explore. Gangs still cause trouble for practice, the Alley Cat Cup is open, and every shop is stocked. Thanks for playing!
dog_offer: Young man! Have you seen my Biscuit? Little tan terrier, red collar, ears like satellite dishes.
He slipped his leash when those hoodlums started shouting. He's always chasing trains. Oh, I hope he didn't go all the way to the rail yard.
I'll keep an eye out, Mrs. Alvarez.
Take his leash. He'll follow anyone holding it. Bless you, dear.
dog_found: A scruffy tan terrier sniffs the leash, sneezes, and wags his whole back end. Biscuit is ready to go home.
dog_return: BISCUIT! Oh, you naughty, wonderful boy!
Thank you, dear. Here, a little something, and empanadas. Don't argue, you're too skinny.
dog_waiting: Any sign of Biscuit? He loves trains. Try the rail yard out at the Ironworks.
tools_offer: You want to help? Some Wharf Rat called Sticky Vic walked off with my red toolbox while I was out looking for Eli.
He hangs around the Canal Walk. Get it back and I'll tape up your weapons for free.
tools_return: My toolbox! Every socket accounted for. You're not totally useless.
As promised: Grip Tape on the house. Your weapons will hit harder and last longer.
escort_offer: Oh, Mr. Vale. My sister lives above the fish hall at Pier Square. I haven't visited in weeks. Those Wharf Rats knock my hat off every time.
If you'd walk with me along the Canal Walk, I'd be ever so grateful. I'd make it worth your while: a first-edition fighting manual.
escort_start: Splendid! Lead the way. I'll stay right behind you. Please don't let them near me.
escort_fail: Mr. Hollis panics and runs back to his bookshop. Talk to him there to try again.
escort_done: We made it! Not a scratch. Well, one scratch. A dignified scratch.
As promised: the Heel Drop manual, first edition, and a little extra for your trouble. Do come by the shop.
parcels_offer: Extra, extra! Read all about... nobody buys papers anymore, mister.
Hey, you look like a delivery guy.
Then deliver THESE back! Somebody swiped three Bellwether Courier parcels and stashed them around town. The Courier pays a reward!
I heard one's on the Canal Walk, one by the Ironworks gate, and one on the Neon Mile. Check crates and trash cans.
parcels_waiting: Found the parcels yet? Canal Walk, Yard Gate, Marquee Strip. Smash stuff! Responsibly!
parcels_return: All three! You're the best courier in Bellwether!
The Courier sent these for whoever found them. Fancy sneakers! You'll run like the wind. Or like a slightly faster you.
score_offer: You! You look like someone with eyes. Pip took my high score on Cabinet 3. NOBODY beats my score. He cheated.
Ask around. Pip, Marv at the snack bar, that kid hogging the back machines. Then tell me what really happened.
score_pip: I didn't cheat! I swear! The stick kept sliding up-left on its own and I got like a ZILLION points.
score_marv: Cabinet 3? Been acting up since Tuesday. Joystick sticks up-left. I wrote it in the service log.
Here, take a look. Nobody reads my logs.
score_teen: Lacey? She played Cabinet 3 on Tuesday too. Her score was weirdly high. She didn't complain then.
score_ask: Well? Did Pip cheat, or what?
score_right: The joystick was broken? So my Tuesday score... was also the joystick?
...Ugh. Fine. Rematch on a fixed machine, Pip. Fair and square.
You've got a good head, Nico. Take my token jacket. Every pin is a high score I earned. Honestly.
score_wrong: Hmm. That doesn't add up, but whatever. Here's a few bucks for asking around.
For the record, Cabinet 3's joystick is broken. Nobody reads my logs.
cup_offer: Step right up! The ALLEY CAT CUP! Three rounds, ninety seconds, bare knuckles. No weapons allowed in Big Mo's alley.
Entry fee's ten bucks. Win, and you take the Champion Wraps home. Interested?
cup_go: Through the alley door, champ! Big Mo's alley is right behind me. The clock starts when you walk in!
cup_win: UNBELIEVABLE! A new Alley Cat champion! Here's your prize!
cup_rematch_win: Still got it! Here's your purse, champ.
cup_lose: Time! Ooh, so close. Talk to me outside if you want another shot.
hub_menu: What do you want to do?
dot_1: Mara's garage is on Brickrow Lane, just east. Eat something first, hon, you look like a stray.
dot_2: The Chain Dogs' lot is at the end of Brickrow. Duke Brannigan used to steal pies off my windowsill when he was eight. Now look at him.
dot_3: Duke's boys came by and swept the sidewalk. SWEPT it. What did you DO to them?
dot_4: Greyline men keep leaving letters under my door. 'Generous offer.' Fifty years I've run this diner.
dot_5: They smashed my window last night, hon. I'm not going anywhere. You hear me? Nowhere.
dot_6: You did it, hon. You brought everybody home. Pie's on the house. Forever. Within reason.
fong_1: Noodles fix everything! Except Wharf Rats. Noodles do not fix Wharf Rats.
fong_2: The Pike sisters sell fish to half the market. Also stolen bicycles. Also more stolen bicycles.
fong_3: You beat the Pike sisters? They still owe me for three hundred bowls of ramen!
hank_1: Otto's crew eats here. Don't start nothin' in my canteen. Start it outside like a gentleman.
hank_2: Otto's quiet for once. Half his crew came in asking about real jobs. Never seen that before.
marv_1: The back room? Employees only. I'm an employee and even I don't go back there.
marv_2: Snack bar's open. The joystick on Cabinet 3 is still broken. Nobody reads my logs.
gus_bait_1: Nico! My brother's shop. Clam chowder's on the stove. Eat, you'll need it out in that rain.
gus_bait_2: They're saying Greyline's finished. My old switch house might reopen. Me? I'm retiring. Fish don't testify.
benny_1: Nico Vale. Still drop your right hand when you jab. Want to learn something new? It'll cost you, nothing's free at Benny's.
benny_2: Victor Rook used to train here. Best student I ever had. Taught the little ones the Oath. 'Nobody fights alone.' Funny how people change.
benny_3: I've got one manual I don't show anybody. Victor's old signature move. The Oath Breaker. I think you've earned the right.
benny_4: Victor asked the judge to keep this place open. Guess he remembered the Oath after all.
hollis_1: Welcome, welcome. Fighting manuals on the second shelf. Please, no fighting near the first editions.
hollis_2: My sister sends her regards, and a fruitcake. I'm afraid it's also a weapon.
rosa_1: Bandages, tonics, smelling salts. Smelling salts in your bag will wake you up if you get knocked out. Trust me, you'll want some.
rosa_2: Business is slower now that people stopped getting beaten up. I'm not complaining. Mostly.
mara_1: Bring me money and I'll make your weapons nastier. Grip tape, chain links, the works.
mara_2: Pier Square's at the end of the Canal Walk. The Pike sisters will sell you your own shoes if you stand still.
mara_3: Victor Rook. Benny's golden boy. He used to fix my bike chain when I was seven. I hate this.
mara_4: Quinn and Mercer Repairs. Eli can't change a tire, but he does the books. Turns out he's good with ledgers.
eli_post: I'm going to spend the rest of my life making this up to everybody. Starting with fixing Dot's window. Badly.
jett_post: Rooftop parkour club meets Thursdays. You're invited, Delivery Boy. Nico. Delivery Nico.
duke_post: One window down, forty-two to go. This squeegee is my life now.
otto_post: We're rebuilding the rail houses. Proper ones. On time, under budget. Turns out I like building better than wrecking.
pikes_post: Legit fish! Freshest on the canal!
alvarez_post: Biscuit and I walk to the diner every morning now. Well. Biscuit walks. I get dragged.
teddy_1: Extra! Extra! Kid hero punches entire Old Quarter! That's you, right? Can I get a quote?
teddy_2: Thanks for the parcels! The Courier says you can have a job anytime.
bigmo_1: Champ! Back for another round? It's twenty-five bucks a win now.
towna_1: I jog this street every morning. Lately I jog it faster. Those gangs are everywhere.
towna_2: Streets are quiet now. I can jog at a reasonable pace again.
townb_1: Greyline offered me twice what my place is worth. My neighbor said no. Then his garage caught fire.
townb_2: Heard they arrested the gray-coat guy. My neighbor's rebuilding his garage. Bigger.
townc_1: Benny's Rec Center is the best place in town. Coach says if you can buy a manual, you can learn a move.
townc_2: Did you know you can pick up a dizzy guy and throw him at his friends? Grab button. It rules.
townd_1: Dot's pie is the only reason I haven't moved. Don't tell her I said that.
townd_2: Whole street's out tonight. Feels like the old days.
price_wait: The ledger, kid. Original only. I'll be at the warehouse.
bus_locked: The River Line isn't running. The Chain Dogs keep jumping the drivers.
ending_cards: Greyline Development's permits were revoked. Its directors spent the next year explaining themselves to a grand jury.
Victor Rook pleaded guilty. At sentencing he asked the judge for one thing: that Benny's Rec Center stay open.
Eli Mercer testified against Greyline. The neighborhood held a pancake breakfast every Sunday until his mother's bills were paid.
Mara Quinn rebuilt the garage. The new sign says QUINN & MERCER REPAIRS. Eli is a terrible mechanic. Mara keeps him anyway.
Jett Vance started a free rooftop club for Neon Mile kids. His grandmother still lives on Velvet Street.
Gus Pereira testified too, then retired to his brother's bait shop. The clam chowder got even better.
The Pike sisters went legit. Mostly. Their fish stand is the best on the canal.
Duke Brannigan paid for every broken window on Kettle Street. Personally. With a squeegee.
Otto Kragg became foreman of the crew rebuilding the rail houses. On time and under budget.
Captain Holt now runs security for the Canal Market. Nobody kicks over the fish.
Officer Price made detective. Officially, she still never met Nico Vale.
And one evening, the Lucky Spoon was full again.
underline_plan: Okay. Look at these manifests. Greyline ships crates to Dockside every single night, but there's not one truck on Floodgate Road.
So how do they get there?
Under it. The Underline. The old subway runs right under the river. Closed since '71.
Kessler Street Station. Jett's rooftops sit right on top of it.
Then go down the fire escape and follow the tracks east. Jett's crew can meet you where the line comes up, at Floodgate Bridge.
And Nico? Bring a flashlight. Bring three.
ul_enter: Kessler Street Station. Closed since 1971. Somebody has been keeping the lights on.
Fresh boot prints. Greyline crates. And... is that a mole with a headlamp painted on the wall?
ul_mid: (a crackling speaker) Attention, topsider. You are in Service Tunnel 3. Nobody walks Tunnel 3 without paying the toll.
My Moles will collect. Mind the third rail.
kowal_intro: So you're the courier. Rook said you'd come down the hole sooner or later.
Paper. Deeds, titles, signatures. Every family in the rail houses signed something on the way out. Greyline likes its endings orderly.
They signed because their houses were on fire.
I dig where they pay me, kid. Down here the dark does half the work. Let me show you.
kowal_defeat: ...Huh. Topsiders don't usually hit back that hard.
The deeds. All of them. They go back to the people they belong to.
Take them. Rook keeps copies of copies. But his trucks don't run without my tunnels, and my Moles don't work for a man who loses.
Service ladder's at the east end. Comes up under Floodgate Bridge. Your rooftop friends are up there. Heard them stomping around all night.
I'm not. I'm retiring. If you ever meet Otis Bell, tell him the Underline's his again.
radio_offer: You look like you can handle yourself. The Neon Saints grabbed my ambulance radio right off the counter. A punk they call Flicker.
Without it I can't call the night crew when somebody collapses on the Mile. He hangs around Big Mo's Alley.
radio_wait: Flicker hangs around Big Mo's Alley, behind the arcade. Be careful out there.
radio_return: My radio! Oh, thank you. Here, take some of the good stuff.
punch_offer: Forty years I punched tickets on this line. Kessler Street to Floodgate, every morning, rain or shine.
When they shut her down I left my brass punch in the crew locker in Tunnel 3. Those Moles probably buried it under their junk.
I'll go through the crates in Tunnel 3.
punch_wait: Tunnel 3. Check the crates. She's brass, about so big.
punch_return: That's her! Still clicks like the day she was made. Tickets, please!
Ruth Kowal let you through? Then maybe this old line runs again someday. Here, for your trouble.
mural_offer: See that wall? That WAS my mural. The canal, the bridge, Dot's diner, everybody. The Chain Dogs keep tagging right over it.
They paint at night in the Chain Lot and sell the leftover cans. If somebody ran them off, I could finish it.
mural_wait: The taggers hang out in the Chain Lot, by the big wall. Two crews, usually.
mural_return: You did it? Okay. Okay! I'm painting you in. Big. With a cape.
weights_offer: Thirty years I sell fish on this canal with an honest scale. Then Greyline 'inspectors' come round and swap my weights for heavy ones.
Now my customers pay for fish they don't get, and they think it's me cheating them. Three inspectors: Pier Square, the Ironworks gate, the Marquee Strip.
weights_wait: Pier Square, the Ironworks gate, the Marquee Strip. Gray jackets with clipboards. You can't miss them.
weights_return: Ha! Look at that, lead in the bottom of every one. Now my scale tells the truth again.
Here. And come by for fish anytime. Honest weight.
ladder_offer: You want real practice? I run a ladder on Thursdays. Nine bouts, nothing off the floor, no crying.
Win and you climb. Lose and you're done for the night, no shame in it. Bout nine is Mae Okafor. Nobody's beaten Mae in six years.
ladder_lose: That's the night. Ice, water, sleep. Come back when you're ready.
mae_intro: So you're Benny's courier kid. He talks about you like you hung the moon.
Gloves up. I'm not going easy because you're nice to old men.
mae_defeat: ...Okay. Okay! Benny, did you SEE that?
I saw it. Six years, Mae. Somebody had to.
Take my wraps, champ. You earned them. Rematch next Thursday.
mae_rematch: Back for more? Good. I've been practicing just for you.
ngplus_card: NEW GAME+. Same streets, same oath. The crews heard about you, and they brought friends.
ines_chat: Night shift on the Mile. Sprains, cuts, and a lot of people who swear they 'just tripped'.
otis_chat: Next stop, Floodgate Bridge. Mind the gap.
kiki_chat: Murals are like neighborhoods. You have to keep showing up for them.
kiki_chat2: Come back next week. The cape is coming along beautifully.
sal_chat: Mackerel's fresh, eel's fresher. Don't ask about the eel.
mae_chat: Benny's ladder runs every night now, by popular demand. Mostly mine.
